overview: The first split most learners make when looking down a microscope: shape.
genZNote: Round versus rod. Pick a lane.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Spherical or round-shaped bacteria; can occur singly, in pairs, chains, or clusters.
aspects.valueB: Rod-shaped bacteria; can be straight, curved, or club-shaped, and occur singly or in chains.

aspects.label: Shape & Arrangement
aspects.valueA: Round cells named by arrangement: diplococci (pairs), streptococci (chains), staphylococci (clusters), tetrads.
aspects.valueB: Elongated cells named by arrangement: single bacilli, streptobacilli (chains), coccobacilli (short, oval rods).

aspects.label: Common Examples
aspects.valueA: Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pyogenes, Neisseria species.
aspects.valueB: Escherichia coli, Bacillus subtilis, Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

aspects.label: Relationship to Gram Reaction
aspects.valueA: Shape is independent of Gram reaction — both Gram-positive and Gram-negative cocci exist.
aspects.valueB: Shape is independent of Gram reaction — both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacilli exist.

aspects.label: Motility
aspects.valueB: Often motile via flagella, though many genera are non-motile.

aspects.label: Spore Formation
aspects.valueA: Endospore formation is rare among cocci.
aspects.valueB: Several genera (Bacillus, Clostridium) form endospores, an identifying feature.

aspects.label: Laboratory Identification
aspects.valueA: Morphology on Gram stain plus arrangement pattern is often the first clue to genus.
aspects.valueB: Morphology, arrangement, and spore stain/motility testing help narrow genus.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Shape narrows the field before Gram stain or biochemistry ever runs.
overlay.memoryTrick: "Cocci" sounds round, "bacilli" sounds like a stick — literally.
